builder_plan.scenario: A self-hosted model uses more compute or memory than your workload can justify.
builder_plan.change: Check for a usable pruned checkpoint and runtime support before attempting model surgery.
builder_plan.baseline: The original unpruned model at the same precision, context, and load.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Task quality, actual GPU memory, serving throughput, and preparation cost.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Adaptive Computation with Conformal Certification
summary: The method replaces uniform full-resolution dense inference (and uniform efficiency techniques such as quantization and pruning) with hierarchical prediction: a low-resolution model proposes regions, conformal risk control certifies which regions contain signal, and computation is spent refining only certified regions. The cost is a two-stage hierarchical architecture plus a conformal calibration procedure requiring labeled calibration data and a chosen risk target, adding pipeline and validation complexity beyond a single dense model. Failure modes include miscertification if the calibration distribution shifts from deployment data, missed sparse signals that the low-resolution stage fails to propose, and speedups that may not materialize on data where relevant content is not spatially sparse.
rationale: The technique is specific to large-scale scientific imaging with spatially sparse targets and requires conformal calibration infrastructure and domain-matched validation, so it merits adoption only if the reader's production workload is in that setting; otherwise it is worth tracking but not yet actionable.

The cost is a two-stage hierarchical architecture plus a conformal calibration procedure requiring labeled calibration data and a chosen risk target, adding pipeline and validation complexity beyond a single dense model. Reported 2.5–72x wall-clock speedup across 3D medical segmentation, 2D galaxy flux prediction, and 1D calcium spike rate tasks, including on commodity CPUs.
